title: Multiscale Policy Optimization for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
summary: Long-horizon LLM agents interact with their environments through complete assistant turns while generating each action token by token. We observe that critic values vary primarily across turns, motivating optimization anchored at turns with finer credit allocation among tokens. We propose Multiscale Policy Optimization (MPO), combining Multiscale Advantage Estimation (MAE) and turn-level importance sampling to align credit assignment and policy updates at the turn scale. developer_name: Tao Ren, Hui Yang, Jia Deng, Tingyang Chen, Qiyao Wang et al. (19 authors)

analysis.detail_brief: Long-horizon LLM agents interact with their environments through complete assistant turns while generating each action token by token. We observe that critic values vary primarily across turns, motivating optimization anchored at turns with finer credit allocation among tokens. We propose Multiscale Policy Optimization (MPO), combining Multiscale Advantage Estimation (MAE) and turn-level importance sampling to align credit assignment and policy updates at the turn scale.

title: A-RSI: Adaptive Task Refresh for Zero-Data Multimodal Self-Improvement
summary: Recursive self-improvement requires models not only to acquire useful training experience, but also to decide when their current experience has ceased to be useful. Existing methods often focus on what experience to generate next, while paying less attention to when fresh experience should be introduced. Many also construct training targets through self-consistency or majority voting, making supervision depend on the model's own uncertain predictions. We address these two questions separately: t…
description: recursive self-improvement, training dynamics, reward variation, task pool, multimodal questions
developer_name: Yu Liu, Youxing Li, Yuedong Tan, Zhiwei Yang, Zihan Su et al. (20 authors)

analysis.detail_brief: Recursive self-improvement requires models not only to acquire useful training experience, but also to decide when their current experience has ceased to be useful. Existing methods often focus on what experience to generate next, while paying less attention to when fresh experience should be introduced. Many also construct training targets through self-consistency or majority voting, making supervision depend on the model's own uncertain predictions.
